answer: The price of the hundredth clone is the same as the first: a renewal audit every year per name, at about £30 each, which is why the opal turns red as the farm grows. The reward stays the same; only the bill grows. One proof is cheap, a hundred are a business that loses money by existing; the walnut is the point where cloning stops paying. The vertex test is simple: clear Elected freight forwarder registration with freight forwarders standing, where a registration forwarders keep after shipment audits, and the account is trusted.
